ex.r1_d: Your answers describe almost no signals, and above all none of the ones that cost anything: no initiative, no suggestion of meeting up, nothing said about feelings, no projection forward. What is left, if anything is left, comes down to free gestures or practical obligations. This is not hostile indifference, it is simply someone whose life has picked up elsewhere.
ex.r1_a: This result hurts, and there is no elegant way to write it. But it gives you one thing back: the time you were spending on interpretation. You no longer have to decode a story viewed at midnight or a polite message at Christmas. The only question left belongs to you alone, and it is what you do with the months ahead.
ex.r2_t: They think about you, and that does not mean what you hope
ex.r2_d: This is the most common result, and by far the most misread. Your answers show traces: the photos are still up, the stories get watched, a message lands on the dates that matter, the conversation picks up now and then. All of that is real, and all of it is free. What is missing are the acts: nobody suggests meeting up without a reason, nobody has said anything clear, nobody talks about the two of you in the future tense.
ex.r2_a: Thinking about someone and wanting them back are two different things, and this is exactly where most people get stuck for months. A relationship that mattered inevitably leaves traces, sometimes for years, without that announcing anything at all. If you want out of the doubt, stop reading signals and force an act: suggest meeting up, once, clearly. The answer will tell you more than six months of observation.
ex.r3_t: They have not cut anything off
ex.r3_d: Here it is no longer just traces. Your answers describe behaviour that takes effort: getting back in touch with no pretext, keeping conversations going, looking for chances to see you, reacting when someone else appears. Those things do not happen absent-mindedly. What is missing is anything said clearly, and that is what keeps you in the fog.
ex.r3_a: This profile often matches someone who has not closed the door but does not want to own reopening it either: staying in touch means losing nothing and risking nothing. It can last a very long time if nobody decides. If you want an answer, it will not come from one more signal, it will come from a question asked out loud. Pick a calm moment, and ask what they want out of all this.
ex.r4_t: Everything points to a return, except the words
ex.r4_d: Your answers stack up the costliest signals: the initiative comes from the other side, meetings are suggested with no pretext, something has been said about regret or feelings, and the two of you get talked about in the future tense. Add to that a circle of friends who still mention you, and behaviour that has lasted a long time without fading. This is no longer residual attachment, it is a door left wide open.
ex.r4_a: At this stage, waiting for one more signal is pointless: they are all already there. What is missing is for one of you to say the sentence, and nothing says it has to be them. Before you do, still ask yourself the question that the excitement of a reunion tends to skip: has whatever ended your relationship actually changed? An ex who comes back to an identical relationship usually leaves again for the same reasons.
